COMMITTEE DISCHARGED AND COMMITTED TO RULES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring out-of-state insurance adjusters employed to appraise in-state property damages arising from emergency situations to employ established rates used for appraisal by in-state insurance adjusters
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S2746

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the insurance law, in relation to
requiring out-of-state insurance adjusters employed to appraise
in-state property damages arising from emergency situations to employ
established rates used for appraisal by in-state insurance adjusters

 PURPOSE :

To ensure that temporary adjusters and insurers are utilizing cost
data that is regionally appropriate.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill amends Insurance Law section 2108(n) to
require independent adjusters issued a temporary permit by the
superintendent of financial services to utilize cost data that is
appropriate for the region of the state where they are adjusting.

Section two of this bill amends Insurance Law section 2601(a) to add a
new paragraph (8) to make it an unfair claims settlement practice for
insurers to either artificially lower cost data used for adjusted
claims or use cost data that is not appropriate for the region of the
state where the loss occurred.

Section three of this bill provides that this act shall take effect
immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Super storm Sandy wreaked havoc in New York resulting in over $60
billion in damages. Thousands of claims were filed and the need to
quickly provide relief to those who lost their homes and livelihoods
forced insurance companies to import hundreds of out-of-state
adjustors from across the country to handle the workload.
Out-of-state insurance adjusters are equipped with computer software
that is supposed to adjust for local cost data to reflect the costs
for repair and construction services in New York State.
Unfortunately, that does not automatically occur and the cost data is
inaccurate. As a result, in many cases, policy holders cannot rebuild
based on the reimbursement received from insurance companies, leaving
them with the choice of either accepting an underpayment for claims or
keep fighting a prolonged battle when the monetary relief is needed
immediately.

If enacted, this bill would help to address the issue of underpayment
of insurance claims by ensuring appropriate regional cost data is used
by insurance adjusters during appraisals to determine the correct
reimbursement amounts to homeowners in order to expedite their
rebuilding efforts after a tragic disaster.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2016: S.6464-A - Referred to Insurance
2015: S.4276 - Vetoed, Memo 228
2014: S.7876 - Passed Senate

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 16 Chapter 458
 
        MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2746, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to requiring out-of-
        state insurance adjusters employed to appraise in-state property
        damages  arising from emergency situations to employ established
        rates used for appraisal by in-state insurance adjusters"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require independent adjusters that are  issued  tempo-
rary  permits  by the Superintendent of Financial Services ("Superinten-
dent") to use cost data that is appropriate for the region of  New  York
where  they are adjusting claims, and would make it a prohibitive unfair
settlement practice for insurers to artificially  deflate  or  otherwise
lower cost data that is used for adjusted claims.
 
  According  to  the Sponsor's memorandum in support, due to the need to
quickly provide relief to those who lose their homes  in  severe  events
such as Superstorm Sandy, insurance companies often utilize the services
of  out-of-state  insurance  adjusters  that  use computer software that
fails to adjust for local cost data. The failure  to  adjust  for  local
cost  data  can  result in policyholders receiving claims reimbursements
that are too low and insufficient to allow  a  homeowner  to  repair  or
rebuild.
 
  While  I understand the intent of this bill is to address the issue of
underpayment of insurance claims by requiring  the  use  of  appropriate
regional  cost  data to determine correct reimbursement amounts to expe-
dite rebuilding efforts after tragic events, section one  of  this  bill
suffers  from  the  same  defects as a nearly identical bill I vetoed in
2015. In Veto Message No. 228 of 2015, I noted that the bill  duplicated
11  NYCRR  Section 216 (Insurance Regulation 64), which already provides
that when no dispute as to coverage exists, it  is  the  duty  of  every
insurer  to  offer claimants amounts that are "fair and reasonable." The
Department of Financial Services has interpreted "fair  and  reasonable"
to  require  insurers  to use cost data for the region in New York where
the real property is located. Section one of the pending bill is  unnec-
essary for the same reasons I stated in my 2015 veto message.
 
  Section  two  of the bill would make it a prohibitively unfair settle-
ment practice for insurers to artificially deflate  or  otherwise  lower
cost data that is used for adjusted claims, or use cost data that is not
appropriate  for  the  region of the state where the loss occurred. I am
supportive of this provision as a consumer protection mechanism.

  As section one of this bill is redundant to existing law, and  section
two provides strong consumer protections against deflated cost data, the
Executive  has  secured an agreement with the Legislature to pass legis-
lation in the upcoming session that would eliminate section one of  this
bill, while keeping section two intact. On this basis, I am signing this
bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Relates to the use of local cost data when adjusting claims; requires an insurer and independent adjuster to adjust certain claims made under an insurance policy that provides coverage for loss of or damage to property using cost data appropriate for the region of this state where the loss or damage occurred.
title: Relates to the use of local cost data when adjusting claims
